 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard repackaging of an upstream GitHub release `.deb` file. It downloads from the project's own GitHub releases URL using a pinned version string and a pinned SHA-256 checksum, so the archive is verified against a known digest before installation. There are no unexpected network requests, no obfuscated commands, and no eval/base64/curl-piped-to-shell constructs.

The `package()` function extracts only `data.tar.*` from the `.deb` using `bsdtar` and unpacks it into `$pkgdir`. This is the normal, expected way to repackage a Debian binary package in Arch Linux. No maintainer scripts from the `.deb` are executed, and no system files are modified outside the packaging workflow. The `depends` and `optdepends` entries correspond to the application's stated Python dependencies and are not suspicious.

The checksum is pinned, not `SKIP`, which is good. There are no signs of injected or malicious code, data exfiltration, backdoors, or tampering with unrelated files. The file is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practice.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard pinned-checksum .deb repackaging; no malicious or suspicious behavior found.</summary>
</security_assessment>
